feature: Purchase-session -> portal auto-login handoff (Git #1313, Epic #1309 Phase 4): POST /api/public/purchase/portal-handoff mints a fresh single-use, 2-minute signup-exchange token for the account created THROUGH the session's own flow — and refuses everything else (invalid/unknown/unpaid sessions, sessions that never completed account creation).
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the #1313 backend mechanism only — no UI is wired to this route yet (Buy.tsx wiring is Phase 8, #1309). The session minted per run is the genuine PUBLIC intake (POST /api/public/checkout-session), same accepted side effect as marketing/read-consent-flow.json's CREATE; it expires in 24h and is never paid, so no account or token is ever created by this manifest.

WHAT CANNOT BE ASSERTED HERE, honestly: the paid + completed-account happy path (mint succeeds, portalUrl carries ?signupToken=...). Reaching it requires a real Stripe-paid session plus the emailed six-digit code — the same architectural wall marketing/read-consent-flow.json and auth/signup-exchange.json carve out. That path, and every eligibility refusal on a PAID session (account_not_completed, email_not_verified, email_mismatch, password_not_set, and the already_set never-records rule), is covered by integration tests against real local Postgres in artifacts/api-server/src/lib/purchase-account-flow.test.ts ('portal handoff' describe block).

The EXCHANGE side of the handoff (POST /api/auth/signup-exchange trading the minted token for a real session, single-use guard included) is covered by test-manifests/auth/signup-exchange.json — this manifest deliberately does not duplicate it.
PRODUCT SLUG architect-essentials-retainer is a real catalog row, confirmed by marketing/read-consent-flow.json against the live services table.

RAN via shaneapp://runTest at authoring time (2026-08-25): 1/5 passed. The CREATE step passed for real; the four portal-handoff steps failed with 404 Cannot POST /api/public/purchase/portal-handoff — the dev api-server on :8080 is serving a build that predates this route (undeployed worktree code, the same expected honest result auth/signup-exchange.json records for its own seed route). Re-run after the next dev-server cycle rebuilds api-server to get the real green.
